items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: But his first influence was Grover and the great musicians in that smooth jazz world like Kirk Whalum.

ctx.x: Your faux stride. But as a working musician you have to adapt constantly, especially if you’re in the role of a sideman.

Sure. When I played keyboards with Boney James there was no stride to be had — you didn’t need stride. I just needed sounds, and you know, understanding that he is not a bebopper. But his first influence was Grover and the great musicians in that smooth jazz world like Kirk Whalum. I mean all these wonderful musicians that are playing in an artificial format but it’s just funk music, it’s just an instrumental pop music is all it is. And so as a New Orleans musician I’ve played many different styles. I’ve played…

I’m going to turn to a question around that I asked earlier about why of five piano players does one get the gig. What would cause you, if you had a steady gig somewhere and you had sidemen and sidewomen, what would cause you to fire somebody?
